answer: Age-weighted lottery: an identity gains weight only from consecutive epochs of verified work, rising slowly toward a cap, like climbing toward a summit. Each epoch a random beacon audits a few long-lived identities, and one that stops participating falls toward its nadir, losing weight faster than it gained it. A Sybil attacker must keep many fake identities continuously active for many epochs, paying steady work for each, while honest users gain weight by staying present. Fresh identities get almost no weight and cannot win or vouch until they age through real work.
